Review: after reviewing a changed manifest and source, run `benmore mcp review <appdir> --reviewed`. It replaces the manifest's digests atomically after the source configuration and canonical binding checks pass. This is an explicit source attestation, not automatic semantic review or an access/operation approval: it opens no app database, starts no workers and leaves owner switches and grants unchanged. Never re-attest unreviewed edits merely to bypass a digest failure. How it writes the file: `review_serialization`.

Local checks: `benmore mcp inspect <appdir> --json` and `benmore mcp check <appdir>` are read-only source checks. They open no database, run no migration and start no handler or app worker. They report the CRUD, request, event, scheduled, command, artifact and UI candidates and the reviewed schemas, and list under `unmeasured` what a source check cannot see (the physical database and pending migrations, environment-dependent routes, current grant/role/tenant authority, host and client acceptance). Exit 0 means the declared source scope passed, not runtime acceptance. Both refuse a manifest whose review is stale with `mcp.yaml: reviewed contract or execution digest mismatch`. `--summary` prints a short text instead of the document: connector.check_summary.

Inspect inventory: `benmore mcp inspect` classifies each inventory entry as exposed, command (a command flow bound to a reviewed command tool, reported with binding `command:<flow>`, effect class and approval mode), command-only (a canonical route with no reviewed native binding), unresolved or disabled; a native table.update declaration is disabled with the reason "v1 exposes writes only through approved commands".
Desktop sidecars: review, inspect and check ignore desktop metadata sidecars (.DS_Store, `._*`, Thumbs.db) in static/ and flows/, which deploy never ships, and the execution digest skips them.

Execution digest: it has two forms. A mcp.yaml with the top-level key `execution_sources: runtime` (written by `benmore mcp review` and the starter, and bound into the contract digest) binds only what the runtime can load, execute or serve: static/, flows/, partials/, layouts/, i18n/, migrations/, emails/, templates/, the root config and schema files (app, encrypted, hooks, workflows, cron, flows, validators, admin, computed, retention yaml, schema.prisma/sql/yaml), seeds.sql, head.html, theme.css, tsconfig.json, package.json, favicon.ico/png and root *.html pages, plus each connections[].openapi document and the JSON/YAML files in its directory. docs/, root *.md, src/, tests/ and hidden directories outside those trees (.sdd/, docs/x/.verify/) do not move the digest, nor do pull-denied files inside partials/, layouts/, i18n/ and migrations/. A case variant of a runtime source name (App.yaml, Static/) or an entry of the wrong kind is refused. A manifest without the key keeps validating against the whole tree until `benmore mcp review` is run again, so a runtime upgrade never turns a reviewed connector off; the stale-review notice says so.

Reviewed source at run time: an app with a reviewed mcp.yaml loads everything the digest covers (flows, schema and migrations, hooks, workflows, cron, pages, partials, layouts, static files, translations, validators, admin, computed, retention, versioning and aggregate settings, and the group, scope, access, role and encryption configuration) from one captured copy of the reviewed bytes, including the absence of a file. A file replaced, removed or added after the load changes nothing until the next reload, and a reload whose source fails a check keeps the previous generation; that is not a database rollback, so a migration that already ran stays applied. Malformed retention declarations and partial computed declarations refuse the load; malformed translation YAML fails before any database change, and removed translations clear on reload. A flow email `template:` is read from the digested bytes (a file outside the runtime sources is not found) and a hook email template stays under emails/.

Migrations with a loaded manifest: while a reviewed mcp.yaml is loaded, a schema.prisma change migrates without writing a migrations/ file. The generated migration SQL and its rollback are kept in the database, so start-up never changes the reviewed source and rollback history travels with database backups and restores. schema.yaml is expanded in memory only when schema.prisma and schema.sql are absent. An app with no mcp.yaml loaded keeps writing migrations/.

One generation per request: each connector request runs against one loaded generation of the manifest, access rules, flows, source and environment. When a reload publishes a new generation, a private read still in flight fails closed instead of returning its result.

Uncompilable command flow: a deployed command flow that the running framework cannot compile (for example after an upgrade tightens command rules) disables only the connector: the app keeps loading with the connector withheld and the reason logged, while benmore check, review and the write gate still refuse the file.

OpenAPI candidates: `benmore mcp generate <appdir> --openapi <file> --out <file>` reads a pinned local OpenAPI 3.0/3.1 JSON/YAML document inside appdir, resolves only local reviewed-file references and records exact read-byte hashes. A pinned document or reference that names a file the execution digest excludes (env.yaml, secrets.yaml, .env*, *.key, *.pem, data.db*, uploads/, .benmore/, .git/ and the other excluded tool directories) or mcp.yaml itself is refused, so its bytes never reach a candidate. It creates only the explicit new JSON candidate output (existing parent, 0600, no overwrite, no live mcp.yaml), with every operation disabled and handler/connection, permissions, effects, approval, idempotency, reconciliation, projection and component review unresolved. Candidate files are not accepted live manifests. Paths for flags are relative to the invoking directory and the OpenAPI input must stay inside appdir. Candidate output inside reviewed app source changes its execution digest and requires renewed review; an external output leaves source unchanged.

OpenAPI schemas: supported schemas use the same strict native subset as manifest schemas. Annotation-only keywords (format, title, example(s), deprecated, readOnly/writeOnly, externalDocs, xml, $comment, contentMediaType/contentEncoding) are dropped from the generated schema, and a nullable optional object property (`nullable: true` or `type: [X, "null"]`) in a request or parameter schema becomes plain optional X, while a required or response nullable property is refused by name. Unsupported forms (including unions, dynamic base URIs, custom dialects, callbacks/webhooks, response ranges, recursive references and ref siblings) fail instead of weakening contracts.

OpenAPI bounds: 8 MiB/file, 64 MiB source, 64 files, 32 reference levels, 100000 expanded nodes, 8 MiB expanded strings/output. When a manifest loads, the file and source bounds cover all of its connections together, each pinned document is parsed and resolved once however many connections pin it, and the node and expanded-string bounds apply per pinned document.

Local server: to exercise a reviewed connector before deploying, run `benmore serve <appdir> --mcp-local [--mcp-writes]`. The resource becomes http://localhost:<port>/api/_mcp and the listener binds 127.0.0.1 only (unless BENMORE_LISTEN is set). Use the host name `localhost`: a request to http://127.0.0.1:<port> gets a plain 404 from /api/_mcp and the /.well-known/oauth-* documents, and no other http origin is accepted as the OAuth resource. The authority directory defaults to a per-app 0700 directory under the user cache dir unless BENMORE_MCP_AUTHORITY_DIR is set, and the connector (and with --mcp-writes approved writes) is switched on through the owner-switch path, audited with subject local-serve; a missing or stale-review manifest stops serve with the reason.
